requirements.title: The bit model defines bit positions, order, and length
requirements.definition: A bit is a binary digit at a numbered position of a nonnegative integer scalar object; bits form w(z-1)...w0, positions are numbered right-to-left from zero, and sequence length is z.

requirements.title: The bit model applies only in bit-intrinsic contexts
requirements.definition: The bit model defines z bits numbered 0 to z-1 only when an object is used as an argument or result of an intrinsic procedure interpreting it as bits; other integer contexts use the 16.4 model.

pending.bit-model-valid-only-for-bit-intrinsic-c: Assert bit-model expectations only through bit intrinsics; arithmetic/value fixtures cite 16.4 and include a mutation preventing bit assumptions from leaking.
pending.other-integer-contexts-use-numeric-model: Assert bit-model expectations only through bit intrinsics; arithmetic/value fixtures cite 16.4 and include a mutation preventing bit assumptions from leaking.

requirements.title: Bit and numeric models need not correspond outside binary nonnegative cases
requirements.definition: The bit and numeric integer models are identical for radix two with leftmost bit zero, but do not correspond for non-binary radix or leftmost bit one; those bit interpretations are processor dependent.

pending.bit-numeric-correspondence-limited: Guard with RADIX==2 and sufficient BIT_SIZE before comparing bit and numeric models for the binary nonnegative case; no portable signed-pattern oracle exists outside that guarded case.
pending.noncorresponding-bit-interpretation-proc: Guard with RADIX==2 and sufficient BIT_SIZE before comparing bit and numeric models for the binary nonnegative case; no portable signed-pattern oracle exists outside that guarded case.

review_rationale: Source registration for Clause 16 general text, 16 through 16.8: intrinsic procedure classes and general rules, the bit and numeric models, atomic and collective subroutines, and the standard generic and specific name tables (batch178). This opens Clause 16. Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds; round 1 found conditional pending plans for the atomic and collective STAT semantics, now resolved into explicit decisions: image-dependent facets are out of scope for single-image fixtures by user decision, and the 'any other error' STAT values have no portable oracle because such an error cannot be induced portably. C1601 and C1602 were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
